As Facebook (FB) Market Valuation Declined, First National Bank Of Omaha Has Lowered Stake by $1.82 Million; Holder West Oak Capital Has Boosted Monsanto Co New Del (MON) Stake
May 25, 2018 - By Peter Erickson
First National Bank Of Omaha decreased its stake in Facebook Inc (FB) by 10.23% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. First National Bank Of Omaha sold 10,361 shares as the company’s stock declined 14.10% with the market. The institutional investor held 90,892 shares of the technology company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $16.04M, down from 101,253 at the end of the previous reported quarter. First National Bank Of Omaha who had been investing in Facebook Inc for a number of months, seems to be less bullish one the $536.75 billion market cap company. The stock decreased 0.27% or $0.5 during the last trading session, reaching $185.43. About 3.28 million shares traded. Facebook, Inc. (NASDAQ:FB) has risen 8.48% since May 25, 2017 and is uptrending. It has underperformed by 3.07% the S&P500.
West Oak Capital Llc increased its stake in Monsanto Co New Del (MON) by 22.9% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. West Oak Capital Llc bought 30 shares as the company’s stock rose 1.12% while stock markets declined. The institutional investor held 161 shares of the agricultural chemicals company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $18.80 million, up from 131 at the end of the previous reported quarter. West Oak Capital Llc who had been investing in Monsanto Co New Del for a number of months, seems to be bullish on the $55.63B market cap company. The stock increased 0.54% or $0.68 during the last trading session, reaching $126.06. About 476,515 shares traded. Monsanto Company (NYSE:MON) has risen 3.06% since May 25, 2017 and is uptrending. It has underperformed by 8.49% the S&P500.
